prompts: Help me write a high retention YouTube intro 0-45 seconds for [title]. The video educates my audience on [specific thing]. Position me as a trusted expert. Grab attention emotionally without overhype. Format into: relatable pain, desire setup, pattern interrupt + unique angle + bold promise, credibility + what to expect.

Help me write a YouTube video script in bullet point format. Goal: educate, resonate emotionally, move viewer to next step (buy/opt-in/watch another). Structure: [video title], main topic, pain-solution-why for each section.

Content market intelligence: Help me find ideas in the [NICHE] space. I'm a one-person business doing [SPECIFIC SERVICE]. I want to be number one in the [MARKET LANE]. Research Reddit, X, YouTube, Twitter. Find: biggest guys, trending topics, gaps where big creators aren't talking.

YouTube script breakdown: Analyze this video transcript [PASTE]. Tell me what works (hook, structure, pacing). Identify what's missing. Break into bullet points by section. Now help me write my version of this idea but applied to [MY UNIQUE ANGLE] using [MY VOICE].

Personal brand positioning: You're a world-class business coach. Help me find my 1-of-1 positioning. I'll give you skills/passions/profit potential. Find three validated business ideas, rank them, recommend the right model. Show me people already making money doing this.
LinkedIn profile audit: Go to my LinkedIn [PASTE URL]. Improve my headline, about section, featured section. Make it clear I'm different, show value to my ICP, position as sales page not resume.

CARE Framework for objection: Clarify they believe the solution works. Ask + isolate: What's the real objection (logistical vs fear)? Reframe: Show them the belief is optional. Empower: Tie them to the decision (identity act), not investment.

I want to think about it / I need more time: Double tie-down. 'So you 100% want this and just want 24 hours to sleep on it?' If yes: 'When we talk tomorrow, if you feel the same, we're 100% moving forward on payment?' Create presupposition of next action before confirming.

What if it doesn't work?: 'Despite [case studies], you're worried you'll be the small percent it doesn't work for? Are you 100% putting in the work? When you hit a problem, will you raise your hand for help?' If yes: 'Then why wouldn't this work for you?' Throw it back.

Partner/spouse objection: 'Is this a respect thing where you've decided and just letting them know, or a real conversation?' If real: Coach them on framing. Wimpy version vs. confident version. Show the contrast. Ask: Which guy convinces his spouse?

Money objection: 'Money aside, do you 100% believe this is what you need?' If yes: Ask three data points (net cash inflow 30 days, cash on hand exactly, credit access). Don't ask 'what can you afford?' Lead with payment options.

Fear-based objection: Normalize. Separate fear from them. 'Which version of you is making this decision: the stuck 5-year version or the future self who's living the life you described?' Identity reframe.

Smoke screen test: If they're still resistant after isolation, deposit close ($0 or small amount). If they won't commit after saying they want it + can afford it + believe it works, it's a smoke screen.
